sq.q: Define declarative programming and explain how SQL represents this paradigm in databases.
answer: Declarative programming focuses on describing what the program should accomplish. SQL is a declarative language because users state what data is needed without specifying how to retrieve it. For example: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > 50000;

lq.q: TypYou are developing a university management system in Java. You need to retrieve student data based on department and marks using JDBC , and you must use declarative SQL queries within an imperative JDBC structure . You also need to explain the JDBC architecture behind this process. Write Java code to do the following: Load JDBC driver Load JDBC driver Establish connection Establish connection Retrieve names and scores of students in 'CSE' department with marks > 75 Retrieve names and scores of students in 'CSE' department with marks > 75 Close all resources Also, explain which parts are declarative and which are imperative. Close all resources Also, explain which parts are declarative and which are imperative.
answer: import java.sql.*;

public class UniversityApp { public static void main(String[] args) { String url = "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/university"; String user = "root"; String password = "admin"; String sql = "SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE department = ? AND marks > ?";
try { // Load driver Class.forName("com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver");
// Create connection Connection con = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password);
// Prepare statement (imperative) PreparedStatement pstmt = con.prepareStatement(sql); pstmt.setString(1, "CSE"); pstmt.setInt(2, 75);
// Execute query ResultSet rs = pstmt.executeQuery();
// Process result while (rs.next()) { System.out.println(rs.getString("name") + " - " + rs.getInt("marks")); }
// Close resources rs.close(); pstmt.close(); con.close(); } catch (Exception e) { e.printStackTrace(); } } }
